title: Priority Signal Optimizer for Private Deploy Requests - segmented runway & comm lanes
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Our current private/VPC/on-prem request intake funnels lots of network-sensitive asks into a manual queue. Customers with intermittent egress, strict air-gapped controls, or complex upgrade constraints experience slow decision cycles and inconsistent messaging. This increases SOC/CE effort and delays revenue for enterprise customers.

Proposal: Build a 'Priority Signal Optimizer' that combines: 1) an automated scoring rubric (network posture, upgrade difficulty, regulatory constraints, strategic value); 2) segmented runway lanes (fastpass / standard / remediation); and 3) templated communication lanes for each segment. The outcome should be predictable SLAs for triage, reduced manual rotations, and a clearer path for engineering to prioritize capacity/engagement. This ticket defines the product spec, scoring signals, and rollout plan for the first MVP focused on networking and airgap constraints.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scoring rubric is documented and stored in Confluence; weights for network, security, upgrade complexity, and ARR influence are configurable.

Automated intake form maps customer answers to scoring signals and assigns a lane (Fastpass / Standard / Remediation) with 95% alignment to existing PM manual decisions in pilot sample of 120 requests.
Each lane has a defined SLA (TTR triage, escalation path) and a communication template for Customer Success and Sales to use.
First pilot (20 customers) shows median triage time reduced by >= 40% vs prior month and engineer handoffs reduced by >= 30%.
Rollout playbook with rollback criteria and a security review checklist is approved by Security and Legal.
Telemetry events for scoring decisions, manual overrides, and lane changes are emitted to the Console for monitoring and auditability.
